title: Cocycle-valid stage of an affine gluing presentation
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme with its selected finite affine gluing presentation $\mathsf G_S$ [def-nagata-finite-affine-gluing-presentation]. Restrict the selected affine overlap data to its recorded finite principal-open covers; retain agreement on their intersections. Fix the raw coefficient tuple $C$ at $c=\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}(S)$ from [def-nagata-affine-gluing-coefficient-stage]; use [lemma-nagata-affine-gluing-coefficients-descend] for the fact that its restricted maps realize the original ones. Use the explicit raw refinement preorder $I(C)$, chart rings, principal-open pieces, restricted maps and fraction comparison maps of [def-nagata-affine-raw-refinement-system]. Its nonemptiness, directedness and chartwise commutative-ring colimit cocones to $A_a=\Gamma(U_a,\mathcal O_S)$ are supplied by [lem-nagata-affine-raw-refinement-cofinal], with colimit understood as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Identify $c$ with the initial tuple $C$ in this preorder. Fix the base point, selected binary upper bounds, auxiliary linear order, and resulting finite-bound function $u$ of [def-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound] on this same preorder.
Form a finite list $E$ of tests from the labelled overlap pieces, keeping both orientations. The open tests are the diagonal cover $W_{aa}=X_a$, the image-in-overlap conditions $p^{-1}(W_{ba})=D(f_p)$, and the domain equations $p^{-1}(W_{bd})=D(f_p)\cap W_{ad}$ on every piece $p:a\to b$ and every chart $d$; all displayed opens lie in the source chart or its displayed piece. Impose these tests also for the reverse-oriented pieces. The map tests are agreement of pieces with the same source and target on their intersections, identity on diagonal pieces, both inverse composites compared with the corresponding chart inclusions, and triple composites compared with direct pieces on their common domains. Inverse and triple comparisons include every finite combination of labelled pieces on which the maps can be composed. Composite domains and their finite principal-open covers are the actual inverse-image/intersection domains of the raw-refinement definition; no composite is asserted to be defined on an entire first piece unless its domain test says so. Cover equalities and piecewise agreement tests are included so that a test does not silently assume that local maps glue.
Here is the exact algebraic meaning of the witnesses to retain. On each affine principal-open test domain with coordinate ring $R[1/t]$, an equality $x/t^r=y/t^s$ is represented by a chosen integer $k\geq0$ and the ordinary ring equality
$$t^k(t^sx-t^ry)=0\quad\text{in }R.$$
This is the fraction equality of [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Compare maps on finite $\mathbf Z$-algebra generators of their finite-stage affine targets and retain the images and all their denominators. For an equality of two finite unions of basic opens in $R[1/t]$, say $\bigcup_iD(h_i)=\bigcup_jD(g_j)$, retain, for every $i$, a positive integer $N_i$ and coefficients $a_{ij}\in R[1/t]$ satisfying $h_i^{N_i}=\sum_j a_{ij}g_j$, and the reverse identities $g_j^{M_j}=\sum_i b_{ji}h_i$, with $M_j>0$. These are exactly the two radical containments by [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], applied in $R[1/t]$ to the ideals generated by the displayed finite lists; an inclusion needs just the corresponding direction. Inverse images of a basic open are computed by the actual restricted ring map, so its image of the basic-open element is used in these identities. Express each coefficient as a fraction and use the preceding fraction criterion to turn each localized power identity into a ring equality, retaining the annihilating power of $t$. Thus open-preservation witnesses here are explicit power-ideal certificates, not arbitrary topological assertions attributed to a ring-colimit lemma.
For each open test $e\in E$, form its two finite basic-open lists already at $c$, using the actual inverse-image maps there. Fix power-ideal certificates for their equality in the original localized chart rings. Choose $w_e\geq c$ containing their finitely many numerator coefficients and satisfying their ordinary ring equalities. The chartwise colimit/cofinality statement above and [lemma-nagata-filtered-colimit-finite-data] supply finite coefficient representatives and equations. To keep the specified representatives rather than replacing them by unrelated lifts, use eventual equality in clause (2) of [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] for each lift and the already specified representative, and pass to a common refinement. Include stages containing every new numerator/domain element in this finite choice. The open-domain certificates persist by applying the displayed transition ring maps.
For each map test $e\in E$, take its actual common domain at $c$, choose finite $\mathbf Z$-algebra generators of its target ring at $c$, retain their fraction-equality certificates, and set $w_e=c$. These certificates exist at $c$ itself: both restricted maps become the same genuine original overlap identification, identity, or composite after inclusion into the original localized chart ring. For any subring $B_a\subseteq A_a$ and $t\in B_a$, the map $(B_a)_t\to(A_a)_t$ is injective, since a fraction $x/t^r$ vanishing in $(A_a)_t$ satisfies $t^kx=0$ in $A_a$ for some $k$, hence the same equality in $B_a$. Apply this also on the principal-open intersections and actual composite domains specified in the raw-refinement definition. Consequently each generator equality at $c$ has the required annihilating-power certificate in its source subring. On any later refinement $B$, for every element $z\in B_b$ of the enlarged target ring, the two compared images of $z$ have equal images in the original localized source ring, because the original overlap maps satisfy the recorded map equality. The same injectivity gives equality in the localized source subring. This proves persistence for the enlarged target without treating the generators at $c$ as generators of $B_b$; the open tests separately identify the domains needed by the gluing axioms.
Define
$$F_S=\{c\}\cup\{w_e:e\in E\},\qquad\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}(S)=u(F_S).$$
By [lemma-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound] there are morphisms $c\to\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}(S)$ and $w_e\to\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}(S)$ in this explicit preorder. Define $\mathsf G_{S,\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}}$ to be the raw datum at this tuple as defined in [def-nagata-affine-raw-refinement-system]: its charts are $\operatorname{Spec}B_{a,\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}}$, its labelled pieces are $\operatorname{Spec}(B_{a,\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}})_{f_p}$, and its piece maps are the restricted $\rho_{p,\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}}$. Comparisons from the raw coefficient datum are exactly the spectra of the subring inclusions and of $x/f^n\mapsto x/f^n$ on localizations, with the commuting squares prescribed there. This specifies the source's refinement/pullback notation; it does not posit an unspecified Cartesian base change between independently enlarged chart rings. Retain all the input choices and the certificate witnesses. The assertion that this datum satisfies all gluing axioms remains the separate downstream eventual-identities theorem, not a dependency used to define its own input.

split_report.summary: Repair of C4/E5: rebase on current node, define the raw refinement category and all chart/localization/piece comparisons in a new statement-only definition, and isolate its nontrivial cofinality in a new statement-only lemma. Expand localized map/open certificates into actual ring equations, use existing fraction and radical definitions plus fixed-representative eventual equality, and define the output by the explicit raw refinement datum. Correct ill-typed pullback language; no common-base Cartesian square is presumed. Two new unsplit nodes, no new Mathlib leaves. Second reading fixes all map-test generator choices at c, proves their certificates there by localized injectivity, and spells out elementwise persistence for enlarged targets; open witnesses use the fixed basic-open lists at c.

For every identity, inverse, open-preservation, and triple-cocycle equation
in $\mathsf G_S$, select a finite stage at which that equation holds on the
chosen generators after localization. Define
$\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}(S)$ to be the selected upper bound of
$\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}(S)$ and these finitely many witness stages. Let
$\mathsf G_{S,\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}}$ be the pullback of the raw datum to
this stage.
